newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Netanyahu telephones Mubarak on summit.
newsitem.headline: Netanyahu telephones Mubarak on summit.

text.p: Israel's Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu telephoned Hosni Mubarak on Thursday to say he was sorry the Egyptian president did not attend the Washington Middle East peace summit, an Israeli spokesman said.
"The prime minister said to the president that he was sorry he did not come to Washington," said Netanyahu spokesman Shai Bazak.
Egypt boycotted the crisis summit in Washington called by U.S. President Bill Clinton after more than 70 people were killed in fierce Israeli-Palestinian clashes.

Israel termed the summit a success but Arabs dismissed it as a failure. Palestinian President Yasser Arafat failed to secure either a target date for a long-delayed Israeli troop pullback from the town of Hebron in the West Bank or Israel's agreement to close a tunnel near Moslem shrines in Jerusalem whose opening sparked the clashes.
The two sides agreed only to continue negotiations, slated to begin on Sunday at Erez checkpoint on the Israel-Gaza border.

Netanyahu briefed Mubarak on the latest political developments with the Palestinians and on planned steps to ease an Israeli siege of the West bank and Gaza that bars travel between autonomous cities, Bazak said. He did not elaborate.
Bazak said the Egyptian president told Netanyahu it was critical for the Arab world that Israel and the Palestinians make progress in Sunday's talks.
Egyptian foreign minister Amr Moussa told reporters in Cairo on Thursday he was pessimistic about the talks.

"The Israeli attitude in Washington has not inspired optimism and reassurance for the negotiations' framework and future, and consequently for the future of the peace process," Moussa said after returning from the United Nations in New York.
